title.narrative: Breaking the Link: Ending Deforestation from Commodity Supply Chains

description.narrative:
Thematic area: Sustainable commodity production Problem to be solved: Unsustainable land use and pressure on forests from global markets/leading companies. Proposed solution (Impact – outcomes - outputs) and target group: The project will reduce tropical deforestation by driving change through agricultural commodity supply chains. It will focus on soy and cattle in Brazil, Colombia, and Bolivia, and palm oil, rubber, pulp and paper, bioenergy, mining, and food estates in Indonesia.
The project will benefit local and Indigenous people by strengthening capacity for forest monitoring; enhancing recognition of Indigenous rights and territories; and protecting forests that support livelihoods. It will connect local and Indigenous leaders to international decision-making processes, both corporate and political. It will ensure women’s inclusion in these processes and in storytelling about the impact of deforestation.
The project aims to help achieve sustainable land use and reduce pressure on forests from global markets, and cuts across NICFI priorities. Outcomes include maintaining historically low levels of deforestation achieved in 2021 in Indonesia, and reducing cattle and soy-driven deforestation by 50% in Bolivia, and by 85% in Brazil and Colombia.
Partners: Satya Bumi (Indonesia), APIB/APOINME (Brazil), and Fundacion EnvolVert (Colombia).
Geography: Indonesia, Brazil, Colombia, and Bolivia. Some activities focus on consumer markets in Asia and Europe.
